Join per-segment attributes to valley cells by position

Source: R/fl_valley_join.R
fl_valley_join.Rd

Takes a delineation, its attribution by fl_valley_attribute(), and a set of stream segments carrying logical attributes (habitat flags, for example), and gives every valley cell the attributes of the segment beside it. This answers "which part of the floodplain sits beside segments with attribute X", which a join on the group key does not.

Usage

fl_valley_join(valleys, attributed, segments, group, cols = NULL)

Arguments

valleys

A binary (0/1) SpatRaster, the output of fl_valley_confine().

attributed

The sf output of fl_valley_attribute() for valleys, one row per group, in the CRS of valleys.

segments

An sf linestring object carrying the group column and the logical attribute columns. Transformed to the CRS of valleys if needed; empty geometries are dropped.

group

Character. Name of the group column shared by attributed and segments, e.g. "blue_line_key". Keys are matched with match(), so they must have the same type in both; an NA key matches the NA group. Segments whose key no row of attributed carries are ignored.

cols

Character. Names of the logical columns in segments to join. If NULL (default), every logical column other than group. Flags stored as 0/1 integers need as.logical() first. The nearest-segment search does not depend on cols, so join several flags (several species, say) in one call rather than one call each.

Value

A list:

nearest

A data frame with one row per attributed valley cell: cell (cell index into valleys), the owning group (a column named after group), dist (map units from the cell centre to the owning segment) and one column per element of cols. The rule for areas.

any

A data frame with one row per attributed valley cell: cell and one column per element of cols, TRUE where any claiming group's nearest segment is TRUE. The "connected to" view.

check

Named integer: valley_cells, attributed_cells (distinct cells inside attributed), missing (valley cells no group claims) and extra (claimed cells outside the valley). Both of the last two are zero when attributed covers the delineation, as fl_valley_attribute(complete = TRUE) does unless no stream cell burns for its fallback (it then reports the cells it left out). The check sees only the union of the claims: a simplified or reprojected copy of attributed can move cells between groups and still pass.

ties

Integer. Cells whose two nearest claiming groups are exactly equally near.

no_segments

Keys of claiming groups with no segment in segments.

Rows of both tables are in cell order.

Details

Each valley cell is claimed by one or more groups (the rows of attributed it falls inside). For each claiming group, the cell takes the attributes of that group's segment nearest its centre. Only claiming groups compete: the nearest segment anywhere can sit on a line the delineation never used (a stream below a network's order floor, say), and that line's attributes say nothing about ground it did not shape.

Where several groups claim a cell, there are two answers, and both are returned:

  • nearest gives the cell one owner, the claiming group whose nearest segment is nearest. Every cell is counted once, so per-group or per-reach areas add up to the floodplain: use it for areas. Exactly equal distances go to the lowest key (numeric order for numbers, C-locale order for text, level order for a factor, NA last), and the number of such cells is returned as ties.

  • any is TRUE where any claiming group's nearest segment is TRUE: ground connected to an attribute through at least one watercourse. A cell can be counted under several groups' flags, so it does not partition.

A nearest TRUE is always an any TRUE.

Joining on the group key instead gives a group's whole floodplain any attribute found anywhere on it. On the Bulkley watershed group's whole-network floodplain (30 m, ff04, by blue_line_key) that read 16,705 ha as sockeye spawning, against 572 ha by position (nearest).

Missing values

A segment's NA is copied as is under nearest, and combined by any() under any (NA unless a claimer says TRUE). A claiming group with no segments has nothing to measure from: it never owns a cell another claimer has segments for, it is left out of any, and a cell only it claims gets NA attributes, dist = Inf and that group as owner. Such groups are listed in no_segments.

Valley cells outside every row of attributed (possible with fl_valley_attribute(complete = FALSE)) get no row, and claimed cells outside the valley are dropped; either case warns and is counted in check.

A cell is inside a row of attributed when its centre is, so the claims of an unmodified fl_valley_attribute() output are exactly the cells it attributed. Duplicate rows for one group count once.

Distances are planar, measured from cell centres with sf::st_nearest_feature() and sf::st_distance(); a lon/lat valleys is refused.

See also

fl_valley_attribute()

Examples

dem <- terra::rast(system.file("testdata/dem.tif", package = "flooded"))
streams <- sf::st_read(
  system.file("testdata/streams.gpkg", package = "flooded"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
precip_r <- fl_stream_rasterize(streams, dem, field = "map_upstream")
valleys <- fl_valley_confine(dem, streams,
                             area_field = "upstream_area_ha", precip = precip_r)
attributed <- fl_valley_attribute(valleys, streams, group = "blue_line_key",
                                  dem = dem)

# A per-segment flag: channels wider than 20 m
streams$wide <- !is.na(streams$channel_width) & streams$channel_width > 20
j <- fl_valley_join(valleys, attributed, streams, group = "blue_line_key",
                    cols = "wide")
#> ℹ 48 cells tied between claiming groups - assigned to the lowest key.
j$check
#>     valley_cells attributed_cells          missing            extra 
#>            28727            28727                0                0 

# Floodplain beside a wide channel (ha): one owner per cell, then any claimer
cell_ha <- prod(terra::res(valleys)) / 1e4
c(nearest = sum(j$nearest$wide) * cell_ha, any = sum(j$any$wide) * cell_ha)
#> nearest     any 
#>  190.55  260.82 

# Joining on the key instead credits each blue line's whole floodplain
wide_keys <- unique(streams$blue_line_key[streams$wide])
by_key <- terra::cells(valleys, terra::vect(
  attributed[attributed$blue_line_key %in% wide_keys, ]
))
length(unique(by_key[, "cell"])) * cell_ha
#> [1] 263.85

# Map it
r <- terra::rast(valleys)
r[j$nearest$cell] <- j$nearest$wide
terra::plot(r, main = "Floodplain beside a wide channel (nearest)")
